chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the Qammatin (merchants of Qumm) entered upon him and said, 'I am your ransom. Livestock, wealth, and trade goods fall into our hands, and we know that your right (khums) in them is established, yet we are negligent regarding it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'We would not be just to you if we made you liable for that today.'

key_terms.أَنْصَفْنَاكُمْ: We have been just/fair to you
key_terms.الْأَبْرَاحُ: Livestock (specifically camels, cattle, sheep, and goats)
key_terms.الْقَمَّاطِينَ: Merchants or traders from the city of Qumm
key_terms.حَقَّكَ: Your right (referring to the Imam's share of khums)
key_terms.مُقَصِّرُونَ: Negligent or deficient in fulfilling the obligation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the timing of paying khums to the merchants of Qumm?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s judicial discretion (ijtihad) in applying the obligation of khums, illustrating a period of respite where the duty was recognized but not yet strictly enforced on the people of Qumm. It underscores the Shia principle of divine justice (adl), where the Imam considers the community's capacity and circumstances before imposing financial liabilities, distinguishing between the existence of the right and the immediacy of its collection.
